major_concerns: Verifier specification coverage may be incomplete allowing unsafe outputs to pass.
Synthetic/derived intent set may not reflect production diversity or edge cases.
Repair-prompt design and stopping rules can introduce bias confounding the verifier effect.
Definition and logging of the "human-intervention" flag is underspecified.
LLM nondeterminism may inflate variance despite paired design.
required_design_repairs: Provide a formal, testable verifier specification (properties checked, completeness/limitations) and include negative-control checks.
Specify human-intervention criteria and independent logging procedure (who/when/why human flagged).
Broaden intent set provenance and document sampling to justify representativeness; include explicit complexity strata definitions.
Publish exact prompts, seeds, retry policy, and repair-prompt templates in the preregistration.
Include pilot variability estimates to confirm paired-power assumptions and predefine handling of model nondeterminism.

major_concerns: Validator coverage may omit operationally-critical properties and bias scores upward.
Benchmark curation choices (topologies, intent types) can induce selection bias and be gamed by pipelines.
Maintenance and licensing of canonical topologies/validators needs attention for public release.
Risk of conflating syntactic proxies with semantic correctness if validators are too weak.
required_design_repairs: Define a validator specification language and coverage matrix; include known-hard test cases and stress tests.
Document topology provenance, licensing, and representativeness criteria; include multiple topology families.
Provide baseline implementation and seed-controlled runs for all pipelines; publish harness, CI scripts, and dataset release plan.
Include adversarial examples and holdout tasks to reduce overfitting/gaming and report validator weaknesses.

major_concerns: Selected iteration bound (e.g., 3) is arbitrary without justification and may bias results.
Unbounded repair policy truncation (wall-clock) can confound comparisons.
Injected fault corpus may not capture real-world fault diversity or correlated faults.
Validators may fail to detect semantic drift/latent harmful modifications.
required_design_repairs: Justify bound selection via a small preregistered pilot or sensitivity sweep and predefine alternative bounds for robustness checks.
Specify and preregister exact stopping rules for the unbounded policy to avoid post-hoc truncation (e.g., max iterations or clear time-limit tied to calls).
Expand and document fault-injection taxonomy with provenance and ensure coverage of correlated/multi-class faults.
Add explicit metrics and automated checks for extraneous/harmful modifications and include qualitative examples in preregistration.

major_concerns: Tool-implementation differences (APIs, fidelity) can confound comparisons between orchestration paradigms.
Fixed model-call budget may advantage some strategies; fairness of budget allocation across paradigms is underspecified.
Ensemble and aggregation rules can bias results if not pre-specified.
Runtime/engineering details (timeouts, parallelism) may materially affect outcomes and are not fully defined.
required_design_repairs: Define a canonical tool interface and provide reference implementations used by all strategies to minimize implementation confounds.
Preregister exact budget accounting rules and equitable allocation schemes (per-step vs. global) and include sensitivity analyses across budgets.
Specify aggregation/consensus rules for ensemble-validator in the preregistration and include robustness checks (e.g., different aggregation thresholds).
Define runtime constraints (parallelism, timeouts) and include logging of call-level metadata to permit reproducibility and post-hoc analysis.
